title: OtoDock MCP package manifest
description: The catalog contract for the manifest.json of an OtoDock MCP package (OtoDock is a fair source project). It accepts every manifest the platform's parser (services/mcp/mcp_manifest_parse.py) and install gate (services/community/community_installer.py) accept, refuses what they refuse where JSON Schema can say it, and adds the community catalog's own rules: a git+ source pins a full commit, a remote source names its endpoint and a non-stdio transport. Unknown keys are allowed at the top level and in every block the parser leaves open: a catalog is additive.
$comment: Custom annotation keywords. x-otodock-since: the platform release that first reads the field; an entry that gives the field a value (not null, empty or false) needs platform_min_version at least that release. x-otodock-floors (on server.source): a list of {pattern, since}; a value matching the pattern needs that release. Validators ignore both keywords.

$schema.description: The schema this manifest follows (this document's $id). Ignored by the platform.

name.description: The canonical slug: the key for assignments, config, credentials and the tool namespace. The install gate takes letters, digits, '-' and '_'; validate_mcp_package and the catalog ask for lowercase ([a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*). Keep it equal to the folder name and never rename a shipped package.

description.description: One line for the catalog card and the agent's tool list.

version.description: "" for an npm or PyPI package (the platform pins the installed release locally); the image tag for a docker runtime; the release a git+ source pins. Required non-empty for a docker runtime and a git+ source.

category.description: core and custom ship with the platform; a catalog entry is community.

server_name.description: The mcpServers key and tool namespace when it must differ from name (defaults to name).

author.description: Who wrote the server code the entry wraps, as its home shows it. Empty on bundled manifests.

author_url.description: Where that code lives (https://..., the repository or the vendor's MCP page). The catalog's registry generator refuses a value that does not start with https://.

config.description: Admin-managed settings shown on the MCP's page. From 1.8.0 a non-empty default is in effect until an admin saves a value (older platforms deliver only saved values).

env.description: Static environment variables (template tokens such as ${mcp_dir} allowed).

path_env.description: Path-bearing environment variables by role. An entry that sets neither or both of role/values, or names an unknown role, is skipped at parse with a warning (not refused).

assignment_mode.description: auto (managers enable it per agent, the default) or explicit (an admin assigns it through an instance). Not validated by the parser.

exclude_from.description: Session contexts that never load the MCP: phone, task, terminal, meeting, external. Values are not validated; an unknown word excludes nothing.

audience.description: The tier of the agent this whole MCP is for (empty admits everyone). A 1.7.0 platform does not read it and admits every tier.

requires_capability.description: A platform feature the MCP needs before it is assignable: audio_transcribe, audio_tts or phone_calls. An unknown token keeps the MCP hidden. Not for community packages.

network_targets.description: The internal hosts a homelab MCP dials; the admin's _network_access toggle opens the sandbox to exactly those. An entry without host_key is dropped at parse.

outputs.description: Files the server writes into a shared folder that the platform moves into the session's workspace after matching tool calls. An entry without source or destination_template is dropped at parse.

skills.description: Agent Skills bundled with the MCP.

agent_context.description: Per-session prompt blocks with ${ns.key} tokens. Strict: an unknown key in a block or its builder refuses the manifest.

always_load.description: Direct-LLM deferred tool loading opt-out (strict bool, default false).

placement.description: Device-local MCP class. Not for community packages.

device_capability.description: Marks a device-control MCP. Not for community packages.

device_high_risk_tools.description: Tools pinned to the critical permission tier. Not for community packages.

replaces.description: The sources this entry supersedes, with the credential keys the new source renames. Information for the admin's switch, never an authorization. An entry carries it when its source changed: 1.6 and older converge onto the new source unasked and 1.7.0 refuses the move with no switch, so the entry needs 1.7.1.

patched.description: true when patches/*.patch ship and are applied after npm install.

platform_min_version.description: Catalog metadata: the oldest platform release that may install the entry (copied into registry.json, default 1.0.0). Compared by its leading MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; an unparseable value counts as compatible.

allOf.$comment: _validate_manifest: a community MCP whose runtime installs on the host (python, node) must name its package.
check_package: a docker runtime names its compose file and carries a version (the image tag).
check_package: a git+ source carries a version (the release its ref pins).
mcp_validate_oauth: bearer_required needs a streamable-HTTP transport (sse refused since 1.7.1).
_validate_authorization_server: an https url_template with a literal host (the host must also match an entry of proposed_hosts, which JSON Schema cannot compare).

_validate_api_key_header: streamable HTTP, a literal http(s) url_template with a host (matching proposed_hosts: not expressible), never beside oauth.bearer_required or hosted.api_key_relay. value_from must name a declared password field or env instance field (not expressible).
_parse_hosted_block: an available api_key_relay needs a relay_path and env-delivered instances.
_parse_manifest: result_files and an outputs entry relocating every tool (after_tools absent, empty or holding '*') are refused together. A tool named by both is refused too (not expressible).

falsy.description: A value Python reads as false (the platform treats it as not declared).

hostPattern.description: A hostname, '*' allowed for wildcard labels (the bearer allowlist's fnmatch rule); no scheme, port or path.

installedRuntimeWord.description: python or node as runtime_of reads them (case-folded, stripped): installed into a venv or node_modules on the host that runs them.

relativeFile.description: A plain relative path to a file inside the MCP folder (skill_file_error): no leading or trailing '/', no empty, '.' or '..' segment, no backslash, no control character, no drive letter, at most 512 characters. The install gate also requires a regular file there (not expressible).

noMasterKeyReference.$comment: check_package: the manifest never references the master key (${platform.api_key} or ${proxy_api_key}), in any string or key.

gitSourceIdentity.$comment: _validate_manifest via _git_identity: the source names one repository. The port of the URL's host (if any) is an integer 0-65535, and the fragment names at most one subdirectory.

gitCatalogPin.$comment: Catalog rule (scripts/generate-registry.py GIT_COMMIT_RE): a git+ source pins the full 40-character lowercase-hex commit of a release, git+<url>@<commit>[#subdirectory=<dir>]. A tag can move upstream with no catalog change, and from 1.8.0 the weekly update builds a git+ entry's new ref unattended.

runtime.description: python, node, docker or none (context-only, no process). A remote (vendor-hosted) MCP declares none. Read case-folded; the parser does not validate the word, the install gate requires the key on a non-remote server.

transport.description: stdio (python, node), http (a container, streamable HTTP at /mcp/), streamable_http or streamable-http (a remote MCP), legacy sse, or none (context-only). Not validated by the parser except where a credential block needs streamable HTTP.

command.description: What to launch for a python or node runtime, relative to the folder (node, venv/bin/python). Required for those runtimes.

args.description: Command arguments; ${mcp_dir} and the other template tokens allowed.

source.description: npm:<package>, pypi:<package> (with one group of extras, pypi:<package>[a,b], from 1.8.0), git+<url>@<commit>#subdirectory=<dir>, docker:<label> or remote:<host>. A catalog leaves npm and PyPI packages unpinned; the platform pins the installed release locally.

docker_compose.description: The compose file of a docker runtime, a plain relative path inside the folder.

url_template.description: A container's base URL (http://${docker_mcp_host}:${port}) or a remote MCP's endpoint (https://mcp.vendor.com/mcp), whose host is its identity.

proxy_callbacks.description: A Docker/HTTP MCP that calls back to the proxy hooks gets a per-session JWT. Not for community packages.

service_name.description: Service-DNS name of a docker runtime under Docker-Compose (defaults to name).

image.description: The pre-built image a containerised proxy pulls (required for the Docker-Compose deployment).

version_constraint.description: A PEP 440 specifier set bounding the automatic updates of an npm or PyPI package (">=2,<3"). An invalid one is read as unbounded.

source_build.description: For a pypi: source, the distributions the installer may build from a source distribution when no wheel fits (SOURCE_BUILD_RE).

allOf.$comment: git+ sources: the platform's identity rule and the catalog's pinned commit.
_validate_manifest: a remote source needs a url_template and a non-stdio transport; any other non-empty server block needs a runtime, and an installed runtime (python, node) a command.

credentials.description: What the MCP needs to authenticate.

type.description: none, per_user (each person enters their own) or infra (an admin enters them once). Not validated by the parser.

service_account.description: A manager may lend an account to agent-scope sessions.

required.description: A field is required unless it declares false (enforced from 1.8.0; older platforms treat every field as optional, so false degrades safely).

oauth.description: An OAuth provider (mcp_validate_oauth._validate_oauth_services). Strict where the validator is; keys it does not know stay open.

bearer_required.description: A remote MCP whose requests carry the bound account's bearer, added by the credential gateway. Needs proposed_hosts and a streamable-HTTP transport.

proposed_hosts.description: The hosts the manifest proposes for bearer injection; an admin approves them.

allOf.$comment: The validator rejects the older singular key and the 'provider' spelling.
Google scopes are URLs under https://www.googleapis.com/auth/ (or openid).
_validate_authorization_server: one PKCE flow, the bearer, an https userinfo_url if any, not a hardcoded provider, none of the keys a registered client cannot use.

authorizationServer.description: The MCP server names its own authorization server (RFC 9728, RFC 8414) and the install registers itself there (RFC 7591). A 1.7.0 proxy accepts the block and ignores it.

apiKeyHeader.description: A header-style API key for a vendor-hosted MCP server, added by the credential gateway on the way out. A 1.7.0 platform loads the MCP without adding the header.

name.description: The HTTP header the gateway adds; never one the platform owns or strips.

value_from.description: A credentials.fields key with input_type password (credentials.type per_user or infra) or an env-delivered instances.fields key.

webhooks.description: A vendor webhook receiver (mcp_validate_webhooks). Validated only when available is true. When credentials.oauth is declared too, its provider_id must equal oauth.provider_id (not expressible).

default.description: In effect until an admin saves a value (1.8.0): a string as written, a number as its text, a bool as true/false; an empty string or any other type sets nothing.

pathEnvEntry.description: Either {role, subpath} (one path) or {values: [{role, subpath}], join} (joined paths). Roles: workspace, user_root, shared_workspace, config, knowledge_dir, credentials_dir (subpath required). Invalid entries are skipped at parse, not refused.

toolArgPaths.description: Which tool arguments carry paths: {"<tool>": {"<json_path>": {mode, optional, relative_anchor}}}. json_path is a JSONPath subset: name, a.b, name[*] and their combinations.

instances.description: Per-instance, per-agent configuration (pair with assignment_mode explicit).

delivery.description: env (default), config_file or none. Not validated by the parser.

input_type.description: text, url, number, password, ssh_key_select, phone_route_outbound_select.

source.description: config, instance, per_user_credential or infra_credential (default config).

host.description: Only ${mcp_dir} is resolved; the host must sit under the agent's dir or mcps/.

hosted.description: OtoDock's hosted-relay offering. Not for community packages outside the entries OtoDock maintains.

resultFiles.description: The tools whose pictures and file blobs the platform keeps under subdir of the session's workspace and shows in the chat. An older platform ignores the key.

subdir.description: One plain folder name, not a Windows device name nor inbox, apps or uploads. Absent: the MCP's name when it qualifies, else mcp-files.

id.description: The skill name: lowercase letters and digits in runs joined by single hyphens, at most 64 characters (SKILL_ID_RE). The install gate requires a non-empty string; an id outside the grammar is dropped at parse with a warning.

loading.description: on_demand (default) or always. Another value falls back to on_demand at parse.

audience.description: The tier the skill is for (empty = everyone). A 1.7.0 platform does not read it and gives the skill to every tier.

source.description: A previous source (a package pointer, a container's previous server.image, a hosted MCP's previous host or URL), matched by identity.

credentials.description: Old key to new key, both plain identifiers (no leading '_').

costs.description: Per-tool prices, first matching rule wins.

permissions.description: Per-tool permission tiers, first matching rule wins. A catalog entry gets open honored only from exact tool-name rules.

tool.description: A bare tool name, an fnmatch glob or '*'. An exact name appears once (not expressible).

toolFilter.description: For a container whose server takes a tool-filter regex. The platform writes the admin's regex bare to regex_env_var_name and the flag arg_name '<regex>' to env_var_name in the container's .env (the two names must differ). A no-op on stdio.

regex_env_var_name.description: Default ENABLED_TOOLS_REGEX. Before 1.8.0 the .env carries only the composed flag.

companionApp.description: App-connector block (a running local program). Not for community packages.
